messages:
Ops-Bot: INC-18321 - High queue depth detected on /prod/generate (hotpath). Paging oncall @Ashwin :rotating_light:
Maria: saw a bunch of 504s and client timeouts ~ 11:12 UTC, spike in queue depth metric (queue_len ~ 1200).
Ashwin: I'm oncall, taking it. Looking at autoscaler + pool metrics now.
Liam: fyi I've started pulling the hpa events and pod logs. early signal: HPA not scaling fast enough, pending pod warmup delays.
Ashwin: can you paste HPA describe and pool status?
Liam: here - HPA describe (truncated):
```
Name:           gen-hotpath-hpa
Namespace:      prod
Labels:         app=gen
Annotations:    autoscaling.alpha.kubernetes.io/behavior: {scaleDown: {stabilizationWindowSeconds:300, policies: [...]}, scaleUp: {policies: [...]}}
Reference:      Deployment/gen-hotpath-target ( /spec )
Metrics:        cpu (resource) on pods  AverageValue: 75% -> desired replicas: 6
Min replicas:   2
Max replicas:   10
Events:
  11:09 UTC  Warning  FailedGetScalingTarget: failed to get current value for external metric "queue_length": no metrics returned from external metrics API
  11:11 UTC  Normal   SuccessfulRescale: New size: 6; reason: recommended size from external metrics
```
Ashwin: HPA had trouble reading external queue_length for a few minutes (FailedGetScalingTarget). That explains a delayed reaction. need to check external metrics exporter.
Maria: pool status: gpu-pool-3 shows 2 warm pods, 4 pending (initializing), avg warmup time hitting 45s due to model weight load and cache priming.
Chandra: sharing a snippet from runtime logs - timestamps align with the spike:
```
[2026-08-22T11:10:05Z] gen-runtime INFO request enqueued, queue_pos=1023
[2026-08-22T11:10:06Z] gen-runtime WARN warmup_start model=redwood-v2-13b node=gpu-3
[2026-08-22T11:10:51Z] gen-runtime ERROR warmup_timeout model=redwood-v2-13b node=gpu-3 elapsed=45s
[2026-08-22T11:11:12Z] gen-runtime ERROR request_timed_out req_id=ck_3k2a..., status=504
[2026-08-22T11:11:15Z] gen-runtime INFO fallback served model=redwood-v2-7b req_id=ck_3k2a...
```
Ashwin: OK so two pain points: (A) external metrics pipeline intermittently returned no metrics to HPA -> HPA couldn't scale (B) new pods had slow warmup (weight loading / kv-cache misses) leading to long time-to-ready. Hypotheses: 
- H1: metrics exporter (prometheus-statsd-bridge) rate-limited at ~11:09 causing FailedGetScalingTarget.
- H2: model artifacts were not primed on new nodes, warmup took 30-60s due to disk I/O + quantized kernel JIT.
- H3: routing fallback to smaller model reduced capacity but increased tail latency for some requests.
Chandra: I can repro warmup slowdown on a node with heavy IO. sharing iostat/top: disks saturated during warmup.
Liam: adding kube events around 11:09-11:12:
```
11:09:45 kubectl apply patch -> scale up recommended 4 replicas
11:10:01 autoscaler: unable to get external metric: timeout
11:10:55 pod/gpu-3-7jgk Created
11:11:02 pod/gpu-3-7jgk Pulling image
11:11:18 pod/gpu-3-7jgk Started container
```
Ashwin: Immediate mitigation options: 
1) Manually add replicas to pool (bypass HPA) to reduce queue.
2) Temporarily enable pre-warmed standby pods for hotpath.
3) Adjust routing to increase fallback to smaller model for non-critical customers.
Ashwin: I'm going to manually scale gpu-pool-3 to 8 replicas now.
Ashwin: running: `rwctl pool scale gpu-pool-3 --replicas 8 --reason "inc-18321 immediate scaling - warmup lag"`
Ops-Bot: Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/autoscale-warmup (refer to step 4 for manual pool scaling)
Maria: scaling accepted, new pods are spinning. seeing queue length start to drop from 1200 -> ~420 in 60s. :thumbsup:  
Chandra: also pushed a quick fix to runtime warmup sequence to parallelize weight load (hotfix PR #4128) and increased priming concurrency. will canary to 1 node.
Ashwin: Patch to HPA: add fallback behavior when external metric missing - use cpu metric to scale up until external metric returns. applying patch in canary.
Ashwin: `kubectl patch hpa gen-hotpath-hpa --patch '{"spec":{"behavior":{"scaleUp":{"policies":[{"type":"Percent","value":100,"periodSeconds":60}]}}}}'` (canary in prod-1)
Liam: Important customer impact note: two enterprise customers (org: Archway, ID: arch-77; and Nebula, id: neb-104) reported >30% request failures between 11:10-11:14 UTC. CS notified.
Maria: collating request ids and example traces, will attach to incident ticket INC-18321.
Chandra: Observability followups: capture warmup durations, disk I/O per warmup, exporter error logs for 11:08-11:12, and HPA event history.
Ashwin: Hypothesis tracking status: 
- H1 (metrics exporter rate-limit): INVESTIGATING (Liam owner)
- H2 (warmup disk/priming): PARTIAL MITIGATED (Chandra owner) - hotfix deployed to canary, manual scale reduced queue
- H3 (routing fallback impact): INVESTIGATING (Maria owner)
Ashwin: Immediate next steps / owners / SLA: 
- Liam: dig into external metrics API logs and exporter to see why FailedGetScalingTarget happened (owner, due EOD today).
- Chandra: validate warmup hotfix in canary, measure warmup p95 before promoting (owner, due in 2 hours).
- Maria: compile customer impact report, collect traces, coordinate CS comms (owner, due 1 hour).
- Ashwin: follow up on HPA change rollout and create a small integration test for exporter failure case (owner, due 24h).
Maria: handoff to daytime oncall @Liam at 11:29 UTC — I'm going offline for a meeting. full summary in the ticket. :white_check_mark: 
Liam: ack takeover, will continue investigating exporter. will post timeline and add to RCA doc.
eng-runtime-bot: canary deployment status updated: hotfix #4128 rolled to prod-1 canary node - warmup p95 dropped from 45s -> 7s on canary.
Ashwin: good signal from canary. after validation we'll promote fix cluster-wide and add a prewarm flag to the pool config to keep 2 standby pods for hotpath.
Maria: final note for incident thread: 
- root cause (preliminary): combination of external-metrics read failures causing delayed HPA reaction + slow pod warmup due to disk/priming -> temporary capacity shortfall and queue pileup.
- mitigation performed: manual pool scale, warmup hotfix canary, HPA patch to use cpu fallback.
- customer impact: two enterprise customers with ~30-40% failure window 11:10-11:14 UTC.
Ashwin: closing oncall handoff for this incident. moving to postmortem tracking in INC-18321 doc.
Ops-Bot: Incident state -> mitigated (temporary fixes applied). Please file RCA notes and link to ticket.
Maria: thanks all, great coordination.
Ashwin: Thanks, handing off to SRE for RCA writeup.
